summary.headline: Southborough leaders advanced Neary School roof bid preparations, reviewed the FY27 budget, and discussed exploring a joint fire department with Westborough.
summary.summary: Following the March 2 Special Town Meeting, the Select Board met jointly with the School Committee to map out next steps for the Neary School roof replacement and a five-member building committee. State legislators joined the board to discuss state aid, local option taxes, and legislation affecting town finances. The board also reviewed the FY27 operating budget projection of a 4.9 percent tax increase, considered Annual Town Meeting warrant articles, and voted to decline purchasing a deed-restricted affordable housing unit.

topics.title: Post-Special Town Meeting Neary School project planning
topics.summary: The Select Board and School Committee convened to review results from the previous night's Special Town Meeting, where voters approved the Neary School roof repair and a renovation feasibility study while rejecting other alternative options. The boards coordinated on preparing bid documents before the May 12 ballot vote on the $4.5 million roof bond so construction can start in summer 2026. They also agreed to structure a new five-member building committee without designated board seats to oversee the feasibility study.
key_details: Voters at the March 2 Special Town Meeting approved the Neary roof repair and a feasibility study for renovations.
The $4.5 million roof bond must still pass at the May 12 ballot election before funds can be borrowed.
Superintendent Gregory Martineau and consultant Socotec will draft bid documents ahead of the ballot vote.
The boards agreed in concept on a five-member building committee to evaluate renovation options.
Officials plan to bring a full renovation proposal to a Special Town Meeting in fall 2026.
topics.outcome: Voted unanimously to request that the superintendent prepare bid documents for the Neary evaluations as approved by Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The $4.5 million roof repair and future school renovations are major capital projects impacting town property taxes and school facilities.

topics.title: Legislative update with state delegation
topics.summary: State Senator Jamie Eldridge and State Representative Kate Donahue addressed the board regarding state budget pressures and municipal legislation. Discussions covered proposed increases to Unrestricted General Government Aid, the final phase of the Student Opportunity Act, Chapter 90 road funding, and local revenue options such as meals and vehicle excise surcharges. Board members also raised concerns about inadequate PILOT funding from large non-profit schools, radioactive waste disposal costs, and the need for a special liquor license for the prospective Costco development.
key_details: Governor Healey proposed a modest increase in unrestricted local aid, though state revenues face cuts of approximately $3.7 billion.
Senator Eldridge sponsored legislation allowing towns to increase the local option meals tax by 0.75 percent.
The delegation plans to file a $35,000 earmark request for Southborough's upcoming tricentennial celebration.
Representative Donahue is working with state health and environmental agencies regarding radioactive medical waste impacting town disposal costs.
The town will submit a home rule petition for an additional liquor license required under the lease agreement for a new Costco.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; no formal vote taken.

topics.title: Board and committee appointments
topics.summary: The board interviewed two candidates for a single open seat on the Taxation Aid Committee and appointed Sally Waters. The board also interviewed and appointed Kayla Monzack to the Youth Commission.
key_details: Sally Waters and Michael Scheff applied for the one-year open resident seat on the Taxation Aid Committee.
The board selected Sally Waters based on her application history and volunteer service in town.
Kayla Monzack was appointed to the Youth Commission for a term expiring June 30, 2028.
An interview for the Council on Aging was rescheduled to a future meeting.
topics.outcome: Sally Waters appointed to the Taxation Aid Committee (5-0); Kayla Monzack appointed to the Youth Commission (5-0).

topics.title: Reports on gifts, wastewater, and regional fire department
topics.summary: Board members and the town administrator provided updates on several regional and financial matters. St. Mark's School agreed to a PILOT donation of $102,500 for FY27, including $40,000 toward a new police vehicle. Officials also reported on preliminary talks with Westborough regarding potential wastewater sharing along the Route 9 corridor and exploring a joint feasibility study on regionalizing fire and emergency medical services.
key_details: St. Mark's School will donate $102,500 in FY27, with $40,000 allocated to purchase a police cruiser and $62,500 to the general fund.
Town representatives held preliminary discussions with Westborough on extending wastewater services to Route 9 properties.
Fire chiefs from Southborough and Westborough began exploring a shared feasibility study on regionalized fire and EMS operations.
A formal presentation on the regional fire department concept will be scheduled for March 17, 2026.
topics.outcome: Information shared; regional fire study presentation planned for March 17, 2026.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved consent agenda items A and B without discussion.
key_details: Consent agenda items A and B approved unanimously.

topics.title: FY27 operating budget deliberations
topics.summary: The board reviewed updated figures for the FY27 operating budget showing a projected tax increase of 4.9 percent and a positive levy balance of approximately $400,000. Board members debated whether to accept the Advisory Committee-approved budget, which fully funds two additional police positions, or seek further budget cuts to lower the tax impact on residents. A member of the board argued for holding municipal headcounts flat and offsetting police additions by cutting other department budgets or leaving an administrative vacancy unfilled.
key_details: The draft level-services budget projects a 4.9 percent property tax increase for FY27.
The current budget draft maintains a positive tax levy capacity balance of slightly over $400,000.
Every 1 percent reduction in the tax rate increase requires approximately $580,000 in budget cuts.
The Advisory Committee voted unanimously in favor of the operating departmental budgets as presented.
Debt exclusions are planned on the town election ballot for Neary roof, Trottier roof, sidewalks, and road bonds.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; joint review with the Advisory Committee scheduled for March 10, 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: The FY27 operating budget directly determines property tax rates for residents and sets town staffing and municipal service levels.

topics.title: Annual Town Meeting warrant review
topics.summary: The board examined draft warrant articles for the upcoming Annual Town Meeting. Members supported draft language for Article 9 to allow the town administrator flexibility to shift funds among approved capital items, reviewed a $70,000 water fund meter article, and voted unanimously not to support Article 22, which requested $29,000 in Community Preservation Act administrative funds. The board also decided to remove a proposed cemetery commission warrant article in favor of creating an ad hoc committee, and noted receipt of citizen petitions on a separate finance committee and a plastic bag ban.
key_details: Article 9 includes new language allowing the town administrator to reallocate funds between capital items within the overall appropriation.
Article 10 requests $70,000 from the water enterprise fund for water meter leak detection and replacement planning.
The board voted 5-0 not to recommend Article 22 ($29,000 for CPA administrative expenses) due to a lack of pending CPA projects.
The board chose not to create an official statutory cemetery commission, opting instead for a five-member ad hoc advisory committee for land acquisition.
A citizen petition to ban plastic bags has obtained certified voter signatures for the warrant.
topics.outcome: Voted 5-0 not to support Article 22 (CPA administrative expenses). Final warrant signing scheduled for March 17, 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: The warrant sets the town's legislative and financial agenda for Annual Town Meeting, including capital authorizations and bylaw proposals.

topics.title: Right of first refusal for 39 Meeting House Lane
topics.summary: The board reviewed whether the town should exercise its right of first refusal to purchase a deed-restricted affordable housing condominium at 39 Meeting House Lane. The maximum allowable resale price set by formula is $207,363. The Affordable Housing Trust Fund confirmed it has no interest in purchasing the property, as the deed restriction ensures it will remain affordable to a qualifying buyer through an upcoming lottery process managed with CHAPA.
key_details: The unit at 39 Meeting House Lane is a deed-restricted affordable home with a maximum resale price of $207,363.
The Affordable Housing Trust Fund previously reviewed the property and declined to purchase.
The property will be marketed through CHAPA to income-eligible buyers to maintain its affordable status.
Town staff will verify whether municipal employees or local residents can be granted preference in the resale lottery.
topics.outcome: Voted 4-0-1 (Landry abstaining) to decline the town's interest and waive the right of first refusal.

votes.motion: Request that the superintendent prepare the bid documents for the Neary evaluations as approved by Town Meeting
Appoint Sally Waters to the Taxation Aid Committee for a term to expire June 30, 2026
Appoint Kayla Monzack to the Youth Commission for a term to expire June 30, 2028
Recommend that Town Meeting not support Article 22 (CPA administrative funds) as printed in the warrant
Decline the town's interest and waive the right of first refusal for the affordable unit at 39 Meeting House Lane

public_comment.summary: A resident and Advisory Committee member spoke regarding the FY27 budget, stating that with 80 percent of the town budget tied to personnel costs rising 4.5 to 8 percent, residents should expect an annual tax increase around 5 percent to maintain level services without reducing staff.
